{"timeline":[{"headline":"First Recorded Use of Fleur-de-lis","text":"The fleur-de-lis was first used as a symbol in the 12th century, appearing in the coat of arms of French monarchs.","date":"1100"},{"headline":"Adoption by French Monarchy","text":"In 1211, the fleur-de-lis was adopted by the French monarchy as a symbol of purity and was associated with the Virgin Mary.","date":"1211"},{"headline":"Fleur-de-lis on French Royal Arms","text":"By the 13th century, the fleur-de-lis was prominently featured on the royal arms of France, symbolizing the French monarchy.","date":"1200"},{"headline":"Use in the French Revolution","text":"During the French Revolution in 1792, the fleur-de-lis was abolished as a symbol of the monarchy.","date":"1792"},{"headline":"Restoration of the Fleur-de-lis","text":"The fleur-de-lis was restored as a symbol of the French monarchy during the Bourbon Restoration in 1814.","date":"1814"},{"headline":"Fleur-de-lis in Modern Heraldry","text":"Today, the fleur-de-lis is used in various coats of arms and flags, including those of Quebec and Canada, symbolizing French heritage.","date":"1900"}]}

{"timeline":[{"headline":"Sigmund Freud Develops Concept of Libido","text":"In the late 19th and early 20th centuries, Sigmund Freud developed the concept of libido as part of his psychoanalytic theory. Initially, it referred to specific sexual desire.","date":"1900"},{"headline":"Freud Expands Libido Concept","text":"Freud expanded the concept of libido to include a universal psychic energy that drives all instincts, with its reservoir being the id. This expansion occurred in the early 20th century as Freud's theories evolved.","date":"1910"},{"headline":"Introduction of Life and Death Drives","text":"Freud introduced the concepts of the life drive (Eros) and death drive (Thanatos) as part of his theory of instincts, further developing the idea of libido as a source of all natural forms of expression.","date":"1920"}]}

{"timeline":[{"headline":"Creation of Departments","text":"The departments of France were created on March 4, 1790, during the French Revolution, to replace the provinces with a more rational structure.","date":"1790-03-04"},{"headline":"Establishment of Overseas Departments","text":"In 1946, the French government established overseas departments, which are also classified as overseas regions, expanding the department system beyond metropolitan France.","date":"1946"},{"headline":"Reorganization of Departments","text":"In 2015, a reorganization of the regions of France took place, reducing the number of regions from 22 to 13, which affected the administrative oversight of departments.","date":"2015"}]}

{"timeline":[{"headline":"First Shōnen Manga Magazine","text":"The first magazine dedicated to shōnen manga, Shōnen Sekai, was published in 1895. It marked the beginning of a new editorial category targeting adolescent boys.","date":"1895"},{"headline":"Launch of Shōnen Jump","text":"Weekly Shōnen Jump, one of the most influential shōnen manga magazines, was launched by Shueisha in 1968. It became a major platform for popular series.","date":"1968"},{"headline":"Dragon Ball Debut","text":"Dragon Ball, one of the most iconic shōnen manga series, debuted in Weekly Shōnen Jump in 1984. Created by Akira Toriyama, it became a global phenomenon.","date":"1984"},{"headline":"One Piece Begins Serialization","text":"Eiichiro Oda's One Piece began serialization in Weekly Shōnen Jump in 1997. It would go on to become the best-selling manga series of all time.","date":"1997"},{"headline":"Attack on Titan Serialization","text":"Attack on Titan, a popular shōnen manga series by Hajime Isayama, began serialization in Bessatsu Shōnen Magazine in 2009.","date":"2009"}]}

{"timeline":[{"headline":"Launch of Google Forms","text":"Google Forms was launched as a feature of Google Sheets in 2008, allowing users to create surveys and collect data.","date":"2008"},{"headline":"Standalone Product","text":"In 2016, Google Forms was released as a standalone product, separate from Google Sheets, enhancing its functionality and user interface.","date":"2016"},{"headline":"Introduction of Add-ons","text":"In 2014, Google introduced add-ons for Google Forms, allowing users to extend the functionality of their forms with third-party integrations.","date":"2014"},{"headline":"Material Design Update","text":"In 2015, Google Forms received a major update with a new Material Design interface, improving the user experience and aesthetics.","date":"2015"},{"headline":"Quizzes Feature","text":"In 2016, Google Forms introduced a quizzes feature, allowing educators to create quizzes with automatic grading capabilities.","date":"2016"}]}
